title: Ordered-simplex evaluation of the cone straightening
statement:
Use simplicial sets and ordinary nerves of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent realization and cosimplicial pinched cubes $Q^\bullet$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], and the cone adjunction and enriched diagram categories of [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. Work in fixed universes enlarged to contain all constructions. For $n\geq0$, let $[n]$ be the ordinary category with objects $0,\ldots,n$ and one arrow $i\to j$ exactly when $i\leq j$, regarded as a discrete simplicial category. Let $a:\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]^{\mathrm{op}}\to[n]^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the identity on objects, collapsing every nonempty mapping simplicial set to a point. Write $a_!$ for enriched left Kan extension, the left adjoint of restriction $a^*$, as in [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Define $L^{\mathrm{lin}}=a_!L_{\Delta^n}$ and $U^{\mathrm{lin}}=U_{\Delta^n}a^*$; thus $L^{\mathrm{lin}}\dashv U^{\mathrm{lin}}$ as ordinary functors. For any small simplicial set $K$, set $V(K)=\int^{[m]}K_m\times Q^m$, the quotient of $\coprod_mK_m\times Q^m$ by $(K(\alpha)z,q)\sim(z,Q(\alpha)q)$ for $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$, $z\in K_m$, $q\in Q^r$. Set $(\operatorname{Sing}_Q B)_m=\operatorname{Hom}(Q^m,B)$, so that $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$.

For every map $p:X\to\Delta^n$ and every $0\leq j\leq n$, put $X_{\geq j}=X\times_{\Delta^n}\Delta^{\{j,\ldots,n\}}$ and $X_j=X\times_{\Delta^n}\{j\}$. There is a natural isomorphism
$$L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(j)\cong V(X_{\geq j}).$$
It is natural in $X$ over $\Delta^n$. For $j\leq k$, the diagram map $L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(k)\to L^{\mathrm{lin}}(X)(j)$ is the map $V(X_{\geq k})\to V(X_{\geq j})$ induced by inclusion. For any strict diagram $H:[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$, the canonical fiber isomorphism $(U^{\mathrm{lin}}H)_j\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q H(j)$ identifies the restriction to $X_j$ of the adjoint of $b:L^{\mathrm{lin}}X\to H$ with the $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ adjoint of
$$V(X_j)\longrightarrow V(X_{\geq j})\cong L^{\mathrm{lin}}X(j)\xrightarrow{b_j}H(j).$$
No fibrancy hypothesis on $X,p,H$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.1, displayed tail-realization formula on printed p.79, and Lemma 2.2.3.7 on p.83; use the unreversed vertex labels j (HTT labels the diagram by i=n-j); HTT reading copy in sandbox, archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy result.

proof.text: Compose the stipulated enriched Kan-extension adjunction with $L_{\Delta^n}\dashv U_{\Delta^n}$ from [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction]. The composite Hom bijections give $L^{\mathrm{lin}}\dashv U^{\mathrm{lin}}$. In particular $L^{\mathrm{lin}}$ preserves small colimits: maps from its value on a colimit to $H$ are, by adjunction, compatible maps from the diagram objects to $U^{\mathrm{lin}}H$. Colimits of strict $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams are objectwise, since the structure maps descend uniquely to the colimits of the values. Hence evaluation of $L^{\mathrm{lin}}$ at $j$ preserves colimits. The tail functor $X\mapsto X_{\geq j}$ also preserves colimits: in each degree a set over $(\Delta^n)_q$ is a disjoint union of its fibers, and colimits over that fixed set are computed separately in each fiber. Finally $V$ preserves colimits by the stipulated $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ bijection (equivalently, by its displayed quotient formula). These are ordinary colimits, with no homotopical replacement.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.1, displayed formula; agent expansion of the ordinary colimit reduction

proof.text: First take $X=\Delta^m$ with structure map the monotone map $f:[m]\to[n]$. Write $A=[n]$, $v=m+1$, and $M=A\amalg_{\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]}\mathfrak C[\Delta^{m+1}]$, where the old vertices map by $f$. The statement of [lem-coef-cone-boundary-projective-cells], applied with $S=\Delta^n$ and the collapse $\mathfrak C[S]\to A$, says that the old full subcategory is $A$, there are no maps from $v$ to old objects, and its endomorphism object is a point. The same assertion applies before change of index, with $A=\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$. We identify $L^{\mathrm{lin}}(\Delta^m)(j)$ with $M(j,v)$ directly. For a strict diagram $H$, form the simplicial category $E_H$ with old category $A$, mixed maps $E_H(i,v)=H(i)$, no reverse maps, and endomorphism object at $v$ a point; composition is the diagram action. Functors $M\to E_H$ fixing $A$ and $v$ are exactly enriched natural maps $M(-,v)\to H$. By the pushout property they are functors from $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{m+1}]$ to $E_H$ extending $f$. By the defining cone pushout in [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction], these are precisely maps $L_{\Delta^n}(\Delta^m)\to a^*H$. The Kan-extension adjunction identifies them with maps $L^{\mathrm{lin}}(\Delta^m)\to H$. The bijections are natural in $H$; applying them to the two identity maps gives mutually inverse maps between the two presheaves. They commute with maps of the input simplex, since every bijection is restriction of the same functors.

source.place: Section 2.2.1 cone construction and Lemma 2.2.3.1; agent mapping-out verification after change of index

proof.text: Let $T=\{t\in[m]:f(t)\geq j\}$. It is empty or a terminal interval. Put $B_t=\mathfrak C[\Delta^{m+1}](t,v)$. The subset-poset formula of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] identifies $B_t$ with the cube of subsets of $\{t,\ldots,m\}$ containing $t$ (the last vertex $v$ has been omitted). The mapping set $M(j,v)$ is the simplicial quotient of $\coprod_{t\in T}B_t$ by $z\sim z\circ g$ for $t\leq u$ in $T$, $g\in\mathfrak C[\Delta^m](t,u)$ and $z\in B_u$, in matching degrees. Indeed a composable word from $j$ to $v$ contains exactly one final cone arrow. Compose all preceding old arrows in $A$; the remaining old arrow $j\to f(t)$ exists exactly for $t\in T$ and is unique. Moving an old arrow of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^m]$ past this final cone arrow is exactly the displayed relation, because its image in $A$ is the unique old arrow. Conversely compatible maps out of the $B_t$ satisfying these relations extend to the mixed mapping objects by precomposition with the unique old arrows, and define a functor out of the pushout. Thus there are no further relations. If $T$ is empty the quotient is empty. All operations here are degreewise and commute with simplex operators.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.1, tail formula; explicit mixed-morphism presentation of its simplex case

proof.text: Suppose $T\ne\varnothing$, let $r=\min T$, and let $K(T)$ be the nerve of the inclusion poset of nonempty subsets of $T$. For each $t\in T$ let $K_t$ be its subcube of subsets containing $t$. These subcubes cover $K(T)$: in a chain of nonempty subsets, any element of the smallest subset belongs to every subset. Send $K_t$ to $B_t$ by deleting coordinates smaller than $t$, and then into the quotient of Step 3. On $K_t\cap K_u$ with $t<u$, write a chain of subsets as $I_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq I_q$. Its image in $B_t$ is the union of the chain $g_h=(I_h\cap\{t,\ldots,u\})$ (containing $t,u$) with the chain $z_h=I_h\cap\{u,\ldots,m\}$ in $B_u$. Composition is union, so Step 3 identifies that image with $z$. The maps therefore agree on overlaps. Moreover each $K_t$ map ignores all coordinates smaller than $t$; consequently the glued map factors through precisely the pinching relations defining $Q^{m-r}$ in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], after reindexing $T$ increasingly. This gives $Q^{m-r}\to M(j,v)$.

source.place: §2.2.2, quotient description following Example 2.2.2.5 (printed p.76) quotient description; forward map in the displayed calculation of Lemma 2.2.3.1

proof.text: Conversely send $B_t$ into $K(T)$ by its subset chain and then to $Q^{m-r}$. A Step 3 relation replaces a chain $z$ in $B_u$ by $z\cup g$ in $B_t$ for $t\leq u$. Both chains contain $u$ constantly and have identical coordinates strictly greater than $u$; the pinching relation of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] identifies them. This defines $M(j,v)\to Q^{m-r}$. On each $B_t$ the composite back to $M(j,v)$ is the identity, since deleting coordinates below $t$ changes nothing. On $K_t$ the other composite deletes coordinates below $t$, which is the identity in the pinched quotient. The maps are inverse simplicial maps. Thus for the simplex $\Delta^m\xrightarrow f\Delta^n$, the value at $j$ is $Q^{m-r}$ if $T\ne\varnothing$, and empty otherwise. Its tail is respectively the face $\Delta^T\cong\Delta^{m-r}$ or empty. Finally $V(\Delta^d)\cong Q^d$ explicitly: the class of $(\alpha:[q]\to[d],z\in Q^q)$ maps to $Q(\alpha)z$, with inverse $z\mapsto[(1_{[d]},z)]$. The coend relations show these are inverse. This proves the asserted formula on every input simplex, including constant and degenerate structure maps.

source.place: §2.2.2, quotient description following Example 2.2.2.5 (printed p.76) and Lemma 2.2.3.1; inverse map and coend calculation, without any weak-equivalence assertion

proof.text: Check naturality before passing to general $X$. A simplex map $\beta:[m]\to[m']$ over $[n]$ sends each eligible $t$ to the eligible $\beta(t)$, and sends a subset in $B_t$ to its image under $\beta$, with $v$ sent to the new cone vertex. These maps respect union and hence the relations in Step 3. Under the inverse map in Step 5 they send precisely that same subset to its direct image in the target pinched quotient. By [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], direct image is the cosimplicial map on $Q$, so this is exactly $V$ of the map of tail faces. This also covers noninjective $\beta$: repeated elements are simply removed when taking the image subset. For $j\leq k$ the eligible indices for $k$ form a subset of those for $j$. Precomposing a path by the unique arrow $j\to k$ sends each $B_t$ to the same summand in the larger quotient. Under Step 5 this is the inclusion of the corresponding tail faces followed by $V$. Thus the simplex comparisons are natural both in the simplex variable and in the required contravariant diagram variable.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.1; direct-image compatibility of §2.2.2, quotient description following Example 2.2.2.5 (printed p.76), with the unreversed vertex convention

proof.text: Every small simplicial set $X$ over $\Delta^n$ is the ordinary colimit, in that slice, of all its simplices $\sigma:\Delta^m\to X$ and their simplex operators. To check this without a density theorem, a map out of this colimit is a family of maps out of $\Delta^m$, one for every $\sigma$, compatible with every operator; its degree-$q$ value on $x\in X_q$ is the image of $1_{[q]}$ under the map for $\sigma=x$. Compatibility recovers every other value and proves uniqueness, as well as commutation with the structure maps to the base. The indexing category is small in the chosen universe. Apply the two colimit-preserving functors of Step 1 to this presentation. The isomorphisms of Steps 2--5 commute with every indexing arrow by Step 6, so their inverses also commute and descend to inverse maps of the colimits. We obtain $L^{\mathrm{lin}}X(j)\cong V(X_{\geq j})$. The same construction applied to a map $X\to Y$ over the base proves its naturality in $X$. Taking colimits of the precomposition maps checked in Step 6 gives exactly $V(X_{\geq k})\to V(X_{\geq j})$ for $j\leq k$. The empty diagram gives both sides empty when $X=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma 2.2.3.1, displayed tail-realization formula; elementary extension of the explicit simplex calculation by the universal property of the simplex colimit

proof.text: For the constant structure map $\Delta^m\to\{j\}\to\Delta^n$, the calculation above gives the diagram with value $Q^m$ at each $i\leq j$, empty value at $i>j$, and identity transition maps among its nonempty values. An enriched map from this diagram to $H$ is determined by its component $h:Q^m\to H(j)$: at $i\leq j$ it must be the composite with the structure map $H(j)\to H(i)$; at other objects its component is the unique map from the empty set. Conversely these components define an enriched map, since the indexing mapping objects are discrete points or empty. By the defining simplex description of $U$ in [lem-coef-cone-presheaf-adjunction] and the Kan-extension adjunction, these enriched maps are exactly the degree-$m$ simplices of $(U^{\mathrm{lin}}H)_j$. For a simplex operator $\alpha$, Step 6 makes restriction precisely precomposition with $Q(\alpha)$. Hence this is the claimed canonical isomorphism of simplicial sets $(U^{\mathrm{lin}}H)_j\cong\operatorname{Sing}_Q H(j)$, for arbitrary $H$.

source.place: Remark 2.2.2.11; explicit componentwise representable calculation for the fiber isomorphism

proof.text: Let $e:X\to U^{\mathrm{lin}}H$ be adjoint to $b$. For $\sigma:\Delta^m\to X_j$, the definition of $U$ sends $\sigma$ under $e$ to the enriched map $b\circ L^{\mathrm{lin}}(\sigma)$, with the two adjunction bijections understood. Step 8 identifies its fiber value with the $j$-component $Q^m\to H(j)$. Naturality of the evaluation comparison proved in Step 7 identifies this map explicitly with $q\mapsto b_j([\sigma,q])$, where $[\sigma,q]$ is the image in $V(X_{\geq j})$ of the coend generator from $V(X_j)$. On the other hand the ordinary coend adjunction sends a map $V(X_j)\to H(j)$ to exactly the simplicial map whose value on $\sigma$ is $q\mapsto[\sigma,q]\mapsto H(j)$. Thus the restriction of $e$ to $X_j$ is the specified $V\dashv\operatorname{Sing}_Q$ adjunct, on every simplex and every simplicial parameter. For $n=0$ all tails are the sole fiber and the calculation is just this coend adjunction; empty fibers and the cases $j=0,n$ require no change. All arguments used raw quotients, functors and ordinary adjunctions, so no fibrancy hypothesis was introduced.

lean.statement: theorem ordered_simplex_cone_evaluation (n : ℕ) : Nonempty (Data.{u} n) ∧ ∃ qAdj : V.{u} ⊣ SingQ.{u}, (∀ (K B : SSet.{u}) (f : V.obj K ⟶ B) (m : SimplexCategory) (σ : SSet.stdSimplex.obj m ⟶ K), ((qAdj.homEquiv K B) f).app (op m) (SSet.yonedaEquiv σ) = (SSet.stdSimplex.{u}.leftKanExtensionUnit SSet.PinchedCube.qFunctor.{u}).app m ≫ V.map σ ≫ f) ∧ ∀ D : Data.{u} n, ∃ (e : ∀ (X : Over (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) (j : Fin (n + 1)), (D.Llin.obj X).obj (op j) ≅ V.obj (tail X j)) (i : ∀ (H : OrderedDiagram n) (j : Fin (n + 1)), fiberAt (D.Ulin.obj H) j ≅ SingQ.obj (H.obj (op j))), (∀ (X Y : Over (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) (f : X ⟶ Y) (j : Fin (n + 1)), (D.Llin.map f).app (op j) ≫ (e Y j).hom = (e X j).hom ≫ V.map (tailMap f j)) ∧ (∀ (X : Over (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) (j k : Fin (n + 1)) (h : j ≤ k), (D.Llin.obj X).map (homOfLE h).op ≫ (e X j).hom = (e X k).hom ≫ V.map (tailInclusion X j k h)) ∧ (∀ (X : Over (Δ[n] : SSet.{u})) (H : OrderedDiagram n) (b : D.Llin.obj X ⟶ H) (j : Fin (n + 1)), fiberMap ((D.adjunction.homEquiv X H) b) j ≫ (i H j).hom = (qAdj.homEquiv (fiberAt X j) (H.obj (op j))) (V.map (fiberToTail X j) ≫ (e X j).inv ≫ b.app (op j)))
